_why: A COUNT IS NOT A COMPOSITION. Two sets of the same size are indistinguishable
by count, so a pin that only counts survives the swap that matters: delete a
load-bearing refusal, add a benign passing test to the same module, and the
total is unchanged. Where MEMBERSHIP is the security property, membership is
what gets pinned.
`counts` still guards collection loss (a module that stops collecting, a
selection that silently narrows). `required` names the tests whose
disappearance would be a silent loss of a refusal the project depends on,
plus at least one POSITIVE CONTROL per step so the set is never all-negative
-- a step that pins only refusals is consistent with a build that refuses
everything.
`required` is a SUBSET, deliberately. Listing every name would make this file
churn on every added test and would pin nothing extra: the count already
catches deletion, and what `required` adds is resistance to substitution.
Names are BASE function names. A parametrised test appears in JUnit as
`name[param]`, and the checker matches on the base, so re-parametrising a
test does not break the pin while deleting it does.

_why: Assessed and deliberately NOT given a membership pin. For each, the count
guards what it can (the module still collects, the selection still selects)
and a membership pin would add nothing the module does not already enforce
on itself, or would pin a subject that is not a refusal.
_left_as_counts_only.substrate-proofs: test_substrate / test_opened_substrate / test_mount_relevance / test_mount_root_formats are host-fact taxonomies. Their property is that a mount classification is TOTAL over the observed shapes, and each module already asserts that totality internally (an unclassified shape fails inside the module, not by being absent from a list here). A CI name list would restate a guard the module keeps on itself.
_left_as_counts_only.attestation-proofs: test_config_attestation (87) is a digest/encoding module. Its membership property -- that every posture field is in the digest -- is enforced by its own POSTURE_FIELDS agreement test, which fails if a field is added and left out. That is a stronger check than naming tests here, and it lives where the field is added.
_left_as_counts_only.prod-fix-1: test_approval_expiry_across_preparation / test_attestation_chronology / test_unicode_hostname_taxonomy are boundary sweeps over generated inputs. Their composition is the input space, not the test names, and the input space is pinned in the modules.
_left_as_counts_only.prod-fix-2: test_secret_canary_sweep discovers credential-shaped fields FROM THE DATACLASS and fails if one is unswept. Membership is derived from the source, not from a list, which is the property this whole file is arguing for -- there is nothing to pin here that the sweep does not already derive.
_left_as_counts_only.composed-message-proofs: Already pins five required names inline, in the step, since G13. Left where it is rather than moved here: it is the pattern this file generalises, and relocating it would churn a working guard for symmetry alone.
